name: check_claim
title: Check a legal claim and issue a signed receipt
description: Preview (may change): deterministically checks exact quoted words only against a named part of a text Open Alvary publishes and what Open Alvary's record lists about its status on a date (and whether it is recorded as binding in a jurisdiction), returning a publisher-signed oa-receipt-1 receipt beside the claim. Does not judge paraphrases and gives no legal advice.

citation.description: A citation such as 'Freedom of Information Act 2011, s. 1(1)'. One of citation or anchor_id is required.

anchor_id.description: The part's anchor_id when already held. One of citation or anchor_id is required.

quote.description: Optional exact words the claim says the law uses; at least 40 characters after normalisation unless the quote is the whole of the part's words.

as_of.description: Optional assessment date YYYY-MM-DD, not after today in UTC. Left out, checks status today.

jurisdiction.description: Optional jurisdiction such as ng; asks whether the record is recorded as binding there.

reading.description: Optional sentence this check is meant to support. Echoed beside the receipt; not checked, not signed, not in the claim digest, never logged.

ReceiptAlternative.description: One candidate work or part when a citation is ambiguous.
ReceiptAlternative.title: ReceiptAlternative

ReceiptApplicability.description: Applicability finding recorded on a receipt when a jurisdiction was asked.
ReceiptApplicability.title: ReceiptApplicability

ReceiptClaim.description: Digest of caller-sent checked fields and the date/jurisdiction basis of the check.
ReceiptClaim.title: ReceiptClaim

ReceiptCurrentness.description: Currentness finding recorded on a receipt.
ReceiptCurrentness.title: ReceiptCurrentness

ReceiptFindings.description: Deterministic findings of a Law check: quote match, published words, currentness, applicability.
ReceiptFindings.title: ReceiptFindings

ReceiptKey.description: Signing algorithm and key identifier committed inside the signed receipt payload.
ReceiptKey.title: ReceiptKey

ReceiptNearest.description: Nearest enclosing part when a cited pinpoint was not found in the published text.
ReceiptNearest.title: ReceiptNearest

ReceiptPart.description: Server-resolved part of a published text checked by Law check.
ReceiptPart.title: ReceiptPart

outputSchema.description: Output of the check_claim tool: signed receipt alongside the echoed caller claim.
outputSchema.title: CheckClaimResponse

name: check_currentness
title: Check cited parts
description: Before showing an answer that cites the corpus: for each cited part, whether it is still published with the same words (unchanged), whether a newer text of the same edition exists (newer_version, with the same part's anchor_id there and whether its words changed), whether the span_hash sent is wrong (span_mismatch) or the part is not public (unavailable; with a key, withdrawn instead when its text was public and was withdrawn for a reason that may be told); whether it was in force on a date; and, given a jurisdiction, whether the record binds there on that date (applicability: bound, not_bound or unknown, with the memberships, legal effect or treaty party entry it rests on). Absence of a recorded link or treatment does not prove none exists.

items.description: The parts: each an anchor_id, or a version_id with a locator, with the span_hash you hold, an optional as_of date and, to ask whether the record binds in a jurisdiction on that date, its jurisdiction, such as sn.

Applicability.description:
How a record relates to the law of a jurisdiction on a date (JUR-03, JUR-04), and what that rests on:
the reviewed memberships, the instrument's legal effect and the state's entry in the treaty's party
list. ``binds`` is ``bound``, ``not_bound`` or ``unknown``; whether the text is in force is
``currentness``, a separate question. Never a decision of anyone's governing law.
Applicability.title: Applicability

CheckResult.description:
What became of a cited part: ``unchanged``; ``newer_version`` (a later text of the same expression,
with the same locator's anchor there and whether its words are identical); ``span_mismatch`` (the
hash sent is not this part's); ``unavailable`` (not public now, or never: not told apart); or, only
for a keyed caller, ``withdrawn`` (its text was public and was withdrawn for a reason that may be
told; owner decision, 2026-10-22). Asked with a jurisdiction, ``applicability`` says whether the
record binds there on the date (api.applicable).
CheckResult.title: CheckResult

Currentness.description:
Whether a part was in force at a date (RSV-08, IDT-03). ``basis`` says what the state rests on:
reviewed events covering this provision (``provision``), only the record's status for its whole text
(``record``), or nothing (``none``). A record-level state is never a claim about one provision.
Currentness.title: Currentness

LinkedAct.description:
A public record a checked link names (EDT-01), such as a national act that domesticates a treaty or
transposes a directive.
LinkedAct.title: LinkedAct

MembershipBasis.description:
A reviewed membership an applicable-law answer rests on: its ID, the body, and whether the
jurisdiction was a member of that body on the date asked about: ``held``, ``not_held``, or ``unknown``
when the date falls in an uncertain window of the membership's dates. /jurisdictions/{id} gives its
dates, evidence and review.
MembershipBasis.title: MembershipBasis

RegionalView.description: A regional instrument's legal effect, as its reviewed record states it (JUR-04, DAT-03).
RegionalView.title: RegionalView

StatedDateView.description:
A reviewed date as its record gives it: the date, how precise it is, and as printed when the record
keeps that. A date with no normalised value is never compared with another.
StatedDateView.title: StatedDateView

TreatyPartyView.description:
One party to a treaty as its reviewed record lists it, with the acts of that state that a checked

name: get_anchor
title: Get one part of a text exactly
description: One part of a published text, such as a section or article, exactly: its words, its span as UTF-8 byte offsets, the hash of its bytes for checking a quotation, a citation such as s. 23(1)(a), the official file and the attribution its rights record asks for. Never shortened: a part too large for one answer is refused; read it from the REST text route with its offsets. With a key, a part whose text was public and was withdrawn for a reason that may be told answers withdrawn, not unavailable. The official published copy always prevails; do not harvest a whole Act part-by-part.

anchor_id.description: The part's ID, from a text's structure.

TreatyPartyView.description:
One party to a treaty as its reviewed record lists it, with the acts of that state that a checked

name: get_relationships
title: Get a source's history
description: Whether a source is current and how it relates to other public sources, one step away: what it repeals, amends or commences and the law it is made under, what repealed, amended or commenced it, the treaty or directive it transposes, domesticates, implements or ratifies and the laws that do so for it, what it cites and is cited by, the instruments made under it, and the source in force in its place now when it has been repealed. For case law: each judgment paragraph that cites a provision or another judgment, with the paragraph's words, and how a judgment follows, applies, distinguishes, doubts or overrules another, or was so treated, where a legally qualified reviewer recorded it. Only links a reviewer has checked against the official text; absence of a recorded link or treatment does not prove none exists. A page at a time.

source_id.description: The source's ID, such as ng-isa-2007, from a search.

relation_type.description: Only links of this kind, such as repealed_by, enables, cited_by or overruled_by.

locator.description: Only the citations and treatments of this part of the source, or of a part within it: a provision's locator, such as sec_2__subsec_1, for the judgment paragraphs citing it (relation_type cited_by), or a judgment paragraph's, such as para_12.

limit.description: Links per page, 1 to 100. The default is 25.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous page, to continue it.

AssertionReview.description:
Who confirmed a judgment's citation, or recorded its treatment, at what level, in what role and when:

reviewer's legal qualification (EDT-01).

name: list_changes
title: List catalogue changes
description: Changes to the catalogue in commit order: records added, corrected or withdrawn, text published, legal effects (repeals, amendments, commencements, transpositions and others a reviewer checked) recorded or withdrawn, reviewed memberships of the African Union and the regional bodies recorded, ended or corrected, and members' suspensions from participation recorded or lifted (a suspended member remains one). Filter by jurisdiction, work, type, document class, language or keyword. Pass the returned resume_token next time to get only newer changes. With a key, a record withdrawn because its rights record changed is named by its IDs only; other withdrawals of records no longer public, and a text withdrawn for privacy, name nothing. Reflects catalogue commits only, not every change in a jurisdiction's law.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction IDs, such as ng or rw; a jurisdiction includes its subdivisions, and a body such as aa-ecowas includes changes to its membership and its members' suspensions.

work.description: Source IDs, to follow particular laws.

type.description: Kinds of change: catalogue_added, metadata_corrected, rights_changed, text_version_published, legal_effect_recorded, treatment_recorded, withdrawal, coverage_changed, membership_recorded, suspension_recorded.

class.description: Document types, such as act or regulation.

language.description: Languages of the affected text, such as en.

q.description: Whole words in the title, citation or summary.

resume_token.description: The resume_token of an earlier answer, for only newer changes.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous page, to continue it.

name: list_expressions
title: List a source's language editions
description: A source's language editions with a published text: for each, its texts, the one to read when no date is given, and what the edition is worth as law as its record states it (authoritative, equally_authentic, official_translation, unofficial_translation or machine_translation, with where that is stated; unknown when nothing is recorded); and the instrument's own rule for which version prevails where its language versions differ (language_rule), or unknown. Inspect language authority: unofficial translations are not authoritative, and a preferred text is a reading default only.

source_id.description: The source's ID, such as ng-foi-act-2011, from a search.

AuthorityEvidence.description:
Where an edition's authority or a language rule is stated, or a treaty's party list is shown
complete: a page and the words of the document (``document``), the address of another instrument
(``external``), or the reviewer who recorded it.

ExpressionView.description:
One language edition of a record (API-02 expressions): its public texts, the one to read when no
date is given, and what the edition is worth as law as its record states it, with where; ``unknown``
when the record states nothing. A preferred text is a reading default, never a claim of authority.
ExpressionView.title: ExpressionView

LanguageRuleView.description:
The instrument's own rule for divergence between its language versions (LNG-03, DAT-07), as its
record states it: ``stated``, with the rule, the language whose version prevails when it names one,
where it is stated and the evidence; ``not_stated``, the reviewed copy states none;
``not_applicable``; or ``unknown``, nothing is recorded.

name: retrieve_evidence
title: Retrieve legal evidence
description: Ranked legal evidence for a question, to cite in an answer: each unit is a provision (or a law's title and preamble) with its exact words or an excerpt, its anchor_id, byte span and span_hash, its citation such as s. 23(1)(a), the pages of the official file it is on, links to read it on Open Alvary and the official file's address and hash, what quoting it asks for, whether it was in force (currentness, with what that rests on), the definitions it relies on and why it ranks there. A question that cites a part (NDPA s. 24(1)(a), section 24 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act, Part V of the NDPA), names a page of a law (page 18 of the NDPA), is an Open Alvary or official address, names a law or asks what a term means is routed to that first. Quote only the words given; check cited parts with check_currentness before showing an answer. The official published copy always prevails; do not harvest a whole Act part-by-part.

query.description: The question, such as: when must a data controller report a breach in Nigeria?

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions to search, such as ["ng"]. With two or more, results alternate between them. Without it, every jurisdiction available to you.

language.description: Only texts in this language, such as en or fr.

as_of.description: Only texts in force on this date, YYYY-MM-DD, with currentness assessed at it. Without it, nothing is assumed about the date.

source_id.description: Only this record, such as ng-data-protection-act-2023: then a pinpoint alone (s. 24) or a page (page 18) is read within it.

max_units.description: How many units, 1 to 15. The default is 8.

max_evidence_bytes.description: The most bytes of words, 4,096 to 40,960. The default is 24,576.

scope.description: applicable, with exactly one jurisdiction: also the law that binds there on as_of (today without it): instruments of the African Union and regional bodies it belonged to (reviewed memberships only) and treaties it ratified or acceded to. Each unit then says how it relates to that jurisdiction (applicability: national, regional_direct, treaty_in_force_for_state, unknown and others, with what that rests on), and the answer states what was added and left out. For a place within a national jurisdiction (ng-la), the national law too, and its memberships and treaties.

Applicability.description:
How a record relates to the law of a jurisdiction on a date (JUR-03, JUR-04), and what that rests on:
the reviewed memberships, the instrument's legal effect and the state's entry in the treaty's party
list. ``binds`` is ``bound``, ``not_bound`` or ``unknown``; whether the text is in force is
``currentness``, a separate question. Never a decision of anyone's governing law.
Applicability.title: Applicability

ApplicableScope.description:
The applicable-law scope a request asked for (``scope=applicable``) and the widening it applied, so
that nothing is widened silently (RSV-03): for a place within a country, the country (``within``) whose
law it added whole and whose memberships and treaty consents it assessed; each body the country has a
reviewed membership of, with whether it held on the date (only the law of bodies ``held`` was added),
how many records of regional bodies and treaties were admitted, and how many were left out, by
relation.
ApplicableScope.title: ApplicableScope

AuthorityEvidence.description:
Where an edition's authority or a language rule is stated, or a treaty's party list is shown
complete: a page and the words of the document (``document``), the address of another instrument
(``external``), or the reviewer who recorded it.
AuthorityEvidence.title: AuthorityEvidence

CatalogueMatch.description: A record that matches but has no published text: identity only, never words.
CatalogueMatch.title: CatalogueMatch

CourtQuote.description: The words a court relation rests on, verbatim from its source, with the provision they are in.
CourtQuote.title: CourtQuote

Currentness.description:
Whether a part was in force at a date (RSV-08, IDT-03). ``basis`` says what the state rests on:
reviewed events covering this provision (``provision``), only the record's status for its whole text
(``record``), or nothing (``none``). A record-level state is never a claim about one provision.
Currentness.title: Currentness

EvidenceAuthority.description:
The inputs to the authority signals (RSV-05): the instrument's place in its jurisdiction's
hierarchy (0 is highest), and for decisions the court's relation to the queried jurisdiction's
courts generally (on the question's matter, where it is known), with the court and its bearing on
other courts as its register records them.
EvidenceAuthority.title: EvidenceAuthority

EvidenceBearing.description:
How the decision's court bears on another court, as a reviewed relation of its court register records
it: on ``court``, on the jurisdiction's courts generally (null), or with ``members`` on the courts of
each member state of a regional body; only on ``matter`` where one is given.
EvidenceBearing.title: EvidenceBearing

EvidenceContext.description: What travels with a unit and is never part of its quotable words.
EvidenceContext.title: EvidenceContext

EvidenceCourt.description:
For a decision: its court in the court register that answers for the jurisdiction asked about
(CPR-04), with the court's own review, and how its decisions bear on other courts on the date assessed.
``bears_on`` lists only reviewed relations: nothing is guessed.
EvidenceCourt.title: EvidenceCourt

EvidenceDefinition.description: A definition in force for a term the unit uses (RSV-06, derived): its exact words and span.
EvidenceDefinition.title: EvidenceDefinition

EvidenceLinks.description:
Where to read a unit: ``web``, the record on the website, at the unit when the website shows this
text; ``api``, this exact part of this exact text; ``text``, the whole text it is in.
EvidenceLinks.title: EvidenceLinks

EvidenceQualification.description: A reviewed link that qualifies the unit's work: it was amended, repealed or superseded.
EvidenceQualification.title: EvidenceQualification

EvidenceReference.description: A provision of the same text that the unit refers to by number (RSV-06, derived).
EvidenceReference.title: EvidenceReference

EvidenceRevisions.description: Everything the pack depends on: the same request and revisions give the same pack.
EvidenceRevisions.title: EvidenceRevisions

EvidenceUnit.description:
One unit of legal evidence (RSV-07): which part of which published text, its exact words (or an
excerpt within the byte budget), the hashes to check them, where it is in the original file and
where to read it, what quoting asks for, whether it was in force, and why it ranks where it does.
EvidenceUnit.title: EvidenceUnit

transposes a directive.
LinkedAct.title: LinkedAct

when the date falls in an uncertain window of the membership's dates. /jurisdictions/{id} gives its

MembershipBasis.title: MembershipBasis

RankingExplanation.description:
Why a unit is where it is (RSV-05): the route, each arm's rank, the fused score, the band, the
signals applied and any diversification. Mechanical, never a legal justification.
RankingExplanation.title: RankingExplanation

RankingSignal.description: One documented signal that moved a unit (RSV-05), with its value and effect.
RankingSignal.title: RankingSignal

RegionalView.title: RegionalView

StatedDateView.description:
A reviewed date as its record gives it: the date, how precise it is, and as printed when the record
keeps that. A date with no normalised value is never compared with another.
StatedDateView.title: StatedDateView

link records as domesticating the treaty. Signature alone never binds (COR-01).
TreatyPartyView.title: TreatyPartyView

TreatyView.description:
A treaty's status, as its reviewed record states it (JUR-04, DAT-03). ``parties`` is on the record
and its anchors, never on an evidence unit; an empty list means none is recorded, never none exists.
Beside it, the date the list is complete as of and where that is shown, when recorded: without it, a

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous answer, for more passages.

scope.description: applicable: also the law that binds in the one jurisdiction given on as_of (today without it): instruments of the African Union and regional bodies it belonged to (reviewed memberships only) and treaties it ratified or acceded to. Each passage then says how it relates to that jurisdiction (applicability), and the answer states what was added and left out. For a place within a national jurisdiction (ng-la), the national law too, and its memberships and treaties.

Applicability.description:
How a record relates to the law of a jurisdiction on a date (JUR-03, JUR-04), and what that rests on:
the reviewed memberships, the instrument's legal effect and the state's entry in the treaty's party
list. ``binds`` is ``bound``, ``not_bound`` or ``unknown``; whether the text is in force is
``currentness``, a separate question. Never a decision of anyone's governing law.
Applicability.title: Applicability

ApplicableScope.description:
The applicable-law scope a request asked for (``scope=applicable``) and the widening it applied, so
that nothing is widened silently (RSV-03): for a place within a country, the country (``within``) whose
law it added whole and whose memberships and treaty consents it assessed; each body the country has a
reviewed membership of, with whether it held on the date (only the law of bodies ``held`` was added),
how many records of regional bodies and treaties were admitted, and how many were left out, by
relation.
ApplicableScope.title: ApplicableScope

AuthorityEvidence.description:
Where an edition's authority or a language rule is stated, or a treaty's party list is shown
complete: a page and the words of the document (``document``), the address of another instrument
(``external``), or the reviewer who recorded it.
AuthorityEvidence.title: AuthorityEvidence

LinkedAct.description:
A public record a checked link names (EDT-01), such as a national act that domesticates a treaty or
transposes a directive.
LinkedAct.title: LinkedAct

MembershipBasis.description:
A reviewed membership an applicable-law answer rests on: its ID, the body, and whether the
jurisdiction was a member of that body on the date asked about: ``held``, ``not_held``, or ``unknown``
when the date falls in an uncertain window of the membership's dates. /jurisdictions/{id} gives its
dates, evidence and review.
MembershipBasis.title: MembershipBasis

ProvisionLookup.description:
What a citation's pinpoint names in the works it resolves to: one part, alternatives (never a
guess) or none, with the reason, and when none, the nearest enclosing part that exists.
ProvisionLookup.title: ProvisionLookup

ProvisionMatch.description:
One part of a public text that a pinpoint names (API-04 provision lookup): its anchor, locator and
exact span. /anchors/{anchor_id} gives its words.
ProvisionMatch.title: ProvisionMatch

RegionalView.description: A regional instrument's legal effect, as its reviewed record states it (JUR-04, DAT-03).
RegionalView.title: RegionalView

SearchCoverage.description: What a text search covered: only published texts are searched, never a record's metadata alone.
SearchCoverage.title: SearchCoverage

StatedDateView.description:
A reviewed date as its record gives it: the date, how precise it is, and as printed when the record
keeps that. A date with no normalised value is never compared with another.
StatedDateView.title: StatedDateView

TextHit.description:
One passage of a published text that matches a search (OA-S1, RET-03): the part it is in, a
snippet of exact canonical bytes with its terms marked, and what quoting it asks for.
TextHit.title: TextHit

TreatyPartyView.description:
One party to a treaty as its reviewed record lists it, with the acts of that state that a checked
link records as domesticating the treaty. Signature alone never binds (COR-01).
TreatyPartyView.title: TreatyPartyView

TreatyView.description:
A treaty's status, as its reviewed record states it (JUR-04, DAT-03). ``parties`` is on the record
and its anchors, never on an evidence unit; an empty list means none is recorded, never none exists.
Beside it, the date the list is complete as of and where that is shown, when recorded: without it, a
state missing from the list is unknown, never not a party.
TreatyView.title: TreatyView

outputSchema.description:
A page of a search over published texts' provisions (OA-S1). ``status`` tells no result apart from
a scope with no published text and from a search that could not run.
outputSchema.title: TextSearchPage
